Once upon a time, there was a great debate over whether the future of folding smartphones would be clamshell or book-style, but at least for now, it seems the book-style foldable design has won out.

Samsung's eighth generation of folding phones uses this design, the anticipated upcoming iPhone Ultra is also expected to follow suit, and leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold appear to follow the same trend…

There are two body designs for foldable smartphones, commonly referred to as clamshell and book-style.

The clamshell design is essentially a traditional smartphone folded in half to become a thicker but half-height device, offering a standard-sized screen in a more portable form. The Motorola Razr is one example, and this design evokes the model the company first popularised back in 2004.

The book-style design (increasingly called that for obvious reasons) sees a more square-ish device unfold to become a small tablet roughly the size of an iPad mini. This is exactly the design Apple plans to unveil next month.

Samsung popularised this design with its Galaxy Z Fold line, and the one launched just last month is already its eighth-generation model.

Xiaomi is now also preparing to join the fray with its 18 Fold, which has a camera module bearing some resemblance to the expected look of the iPhone Ultra. Weibo user Peter shared two photos (above), and he reckons this is an engineering test unit rather than the actual production model.

Our sister site 9to5Google points out that this deep cherry colour appears to be designed based on one of the rumoured colour options for the iPhone 18 Pro.
